writeup: TIC 165227846 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.193266 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 9.90 percent dimming of the star's light, while a secondary eclipse was not detected. The eclipse signal achieved a detection significance of 173.4 in the automated search, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 70.1, though the centroid offset of 2.9 arcseconds from the target position warrants further attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. One open question remains: alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true orbital period may be twice the initially measured value, though eclipse timing and pixel confirmation remain consistent with the corrected period listed here.
